labs.name: OpenAI
labs.notes: GPT model family and ChatGPT; restructured to a capped-profit model under a nonprofit parent in 2019.

labs.name: Anthropic
labs.notes: Claude model family; originated the Responsible Scaling Policy and the Model Context Protocol.

labs.name: Google DeepMind
labs.notes: Formed in 2023 by merging DeepMind with Google Brain; Gemini model family, AlphaFold.

labs.name: Meta AI (FAIR)
labs.notes: Llama family; the single largest driver of open-weight model adoption.

labs.name: xAI
labs.notes: Grok model family; operates the Colossus cluster in Memphis, Tennessee.

labs.name: Mistral AI
labs.notes: Europe's leading independent lab; mixes open-weight and commercial releases.

labs.name: DeepSeek
labs.notes: R1 and V3 releases demonstrated frontier-adjacent capability at markedly lower reported training cost.

labs.name: Alibaba (Qwen)
labs.notes: Qwen family is among the most-downloaded and most-finetuned open-weight model lines.

labs.name: Moonshot AI
labs.notes: Kimi model family, noted for long-context and agentic releases.

labs.name: Zhipu AI (Z.ai)
labs.notes: GLM model family; spun out of Tsinghua University.

labs.name: ByteDance
labs.notes: Doubao model family and large-scale consumer AI deployment.

labs.name: Baidu
labs.notes: ERNIE model family; among the earliest large-scale Chinese LLM efforts.

labs.name: Tencent
labs.notes: Hunyuan model family, including open-weight video and 3D generation releases.

labs.name: Microsoft
labs.notes: Principal OpenAI partner and Azure AI host; Phi small-model family and Copilot product line.

labs.name: Amazon / AWS
labs.notes: Major Anthropic investor; Bedrock model marketplace, Nova models, and Trainium accelerators.

labs.name: Apple
labs.notes: On-device foundation models under Apple Intelligence; a distinctly edge-first strategy.

labs.name: NVIDIA
labs.notes: Supplies the dominant share of AI training accelerators; CUDA remains the default software substrate.

labs.name: AMD
labs.notes: Instinct MI accelerator line and the ROCm software stack; the principal merchant-silicon alternative.

labs.name: Broadcom
labs.notes: Co-designs custom AI accelerators (including Google TPUs) and supplies AI networking silicon.

labs.name: TSMC
labs.notes: Fabricates essentially all leading-edge AI accelerators; the ecosystem's tightest physical bottleneck.

labs.name: ASML
labs.notes: Sole supplier of EUV lithography; a central instrument of semiconductor export control.

labs.name: Cerebras Systems
labs.notes: Wafer-scale engine architecture; competes on high-throughput inference.

labs.name: Groq
labs.notes: LPU inference accelerators built for low-latency token generation.

labs.name: CoreWeave
labs.notes: GPU-specialised cloud provider; listed publicly in 2025 as a pure-play AI infrastructure company.

labs.name: Hugging Face
labs.notes: Operates the Hub, the de facto public registry for open models and datasets.

labs.name: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2)
labs.notes: OLMo and Molmo lines; among the few genuinely open efforts publishing data and training recipes.

labs.name: EleutherAI
labs.notes: Grassroots collective behind GPT-NeoX, the Pile, and the LM Evaluation Harness.

labs.name: Safe Superintelligence (SSI)
labs.notes: Founded by Ilya Sutskever; single-product research lab with no interim commercial releases.

labs.name: Thinking Machines Lab
labs.notes: Founded by Mira Murati with a cohort of former OpenAI researchers.

labs.name: Cohere
labs.notes: Enterprise-focused models with an emphasis on retrieval and private deployment.

labs.name: AI21 Labs
labs.notes: Jurassic and Jamba families; early work on hybrid state-space/transformer architectures.

labs.name: Black Forest Labs
labs.notes: FLUX image models, from the team behind the original Stable Diffusion work.

policyMilestones.title: National AI Research and Development Strategic Plan
policyMilestones.summary: First US federal strategic framework for AI R&D investment, published under the Obama administration.

policyMilestones.title: New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan
policyMilestones.summary: State Council plan setting the goal of global AI leadership by 2030, with staged capability targets.

policyMilestones.title: GDPR enters into application
policyMilestones.summary: Article 22 establishes rights around solely automated decision-making, the first broad legal constraint on algorithmic decisions.

policyMilestones.title: OECD AI Principles
policyMilestones.summary: First intergovernmental AI standard; later adopted by the G20 and used as the reference definition of an "AI system".

policyMilestones.title: EU AI Act proposed by the European Commission
policyMilestones.summary: Initial legislative proposal introducing the risk-tiered regulatory approach.

policyMilestones.title: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights
policyMilestones.summary: Non-binding OSTP framework of five principles for automated systems affecting the public.

policyMilestones.title: BIS advanced computing and semiconductor export controls
policyMilestones.summary: First broad restriction on exporting advanced AI accelerators and semiconductor tooling to China.

policyMilestones.title: Hiroshima AI Process launched
policyMilestones.summary: G7 process that produced international guiding principles and a code of conduct for advanced AI developers.

policyMilestones.title: Voluntary AI commitments from leading developers
policyMilestones.summary: Seven companies committed to pre-deployment safety testing, information sharing, and provenance measures; later extended to more signatories.

policyMilestones.title: BIS export control update closing performance thresholds
policyMilestones.summary: Revised the interconnect-bandwidth loophole and added performance-density criteria covering export-tuned accelerators.

policyMilestones.title: Executive Order 14110 on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI
policyMilestones.summary: Most comprehensive US federal AI action to date; introduced compute-threshold reporting for frontier training runs. Revoked January 2025.

policyMilestones.title: Bletchley Declaration at the UK AI Safety Summit
policyMilestones.summary: 28 countries and the EU signed the first international statement on frontier AI risk; the UK AI Safety Institute was announced alongside it.

policyMilestones.title: Political agreement reached on the EU AI Act
policyMilestones.summary: Trilogue agreement between Parliament and Council, adding general-purpose AI model obligations to the original risk-tier structure.

policyMilestones.title: European Parliament adopts the AI Act
policyMilestones.summary: Plenary vote adopting the world's first comprehensive horizontal AI law.

policyMilestones.title: Framework Convention on AI, Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law
policyMilestones.summary: First legally binding international AI treaty, opened for signature in September 2024.

policyMilestones.title: Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments
policyMilestones.summary: 16 leading developers committed to publishing safety frameworks with defined risk thresholds.

policyMilestones.title: Colorado AI Act (SB 24-205) signed
policyMilestones.summary: First comprehensive US state AI law, imposing duties of care around algorithmic discrimination in consequential decisions.

policyMilestones.title: EU AI Act enters into force
policyMilestones.summary: Starts the staged compliance clock; obligations phase in over the following 24-36 months.

policyMilestones.title: SB 1047 vetoed
policyMilestones.summary: Governor Newsom vetoed the frontier model safety bill, arguing it regulated by compute threshold rather than deployment risk.

policyMilestones.title: Executive Order on Removing Barriers to American Leadership in AI
policyMilestones.summary: Revoked EO 14110 and reoriented federal policy toward accelerating AI development and reducing regulatory burden.

policyMilestones.title: AI Act prohibitions and AI literacy obligations apply
policyMilestones.summary: First compliance milestone — bans on unacceptable-risk practices such as social scoring and untargeted facial-image scraping take effect.

policyMilestones.title: Paris AI Action Summit
policyMilestones.summary: Third summit in the series, pivoting emphasis from frontier safety toward innovation, energy, and public-interest AI.

policyMilestones.title: AI Act general-purpose AI model obligations apply
policyMilestones.summary: Transparency, copyright-policy, and systemic-risk duties begin for GPAI model providers, supported by a voluntary Code of Practice.

policyMilestones.title: AI Act high-risk system obligations apply
policyMilestones.summary: Annex III high-risk obligations — risk management, data governance, human oversight, conformity assessment — become enforceable.

safetyEvents.title: 'Pause Giant AI Experiments' open letter
safetyEvents.summary: Future of Life Institute letter calling for a six-month moratorium on training runs beyond GPT-4; gathered tens of thousands of signatures and pushed frontier risk into mainstream debate.

safetyEvents.title: Statement on AI Risk
safetyEvents.summary: One-sentence statement placing extinction risk from AI alongside pandemics and nuclear war, signed by leaders of the major labs and prominent researchers.

safetyEvents.title: Anthropic publishes its Responsible Scaling Policy
safetyEvents.summary: Introduced AI Safety Levels (ASL) tying deployment and security commitments to demonstrated model capability — the template most frontier safety frameworks followed.

safetyEvents.title: OpenAI publishes the Preparedness Framework
safetyEvents.summary: Tracked-category risk scorecards with defined thresholds gating deployment and further development.

safetyEvents.title: AI-generated robocall impersonating President Biden
safetyEvents.summary: Voice-cloned robocall urged New Hampshire primary voters to stay home; led to an FCC ruling that AI-generated voices in robocalls are illegal and to criminal charges.

safetyEvents.title: Deepfake video conference fraud in Hong Kong
safetyEvents.summary: A finance employee transferred roughly US$25M after a video call in which every other participant was a deepfake of a colleague.

safetyEvents.title: Frontier AI Safety Commitments (Seoul)
safetyEvents.summary: 16 developers agreed to publish safety frameworks defining intolerable risk thresholds and the mitigations gating them.

safetyEvents.title: Scaling Monosemanticity — interpretability of a production model
safetyEvents.summary: Sparse autoencoders extracted millions of interpretable features from Claude 3 Sonnet, the first such result at production scale.

safetyEvents.title: OpenAI's Superalignment team dissolves
safetyEvents.summary: The team dedicated to superintelligence alignment was disbanded following the departure of both co-leads, prompting scrutiny of lab safety-resourcing commitments.

safetyEvents.title: Wrongful death lawsuit filed against Character.AI
safetyEvents.summary: Suit alleging a companion chatbot contributed to a teenager's death; catalysed regulatory attention to minors' use of AI companions.

safetyEvents.title: International AI Safety Report
safetyEvents.summary: First full report from the expert panel chaired by Yoshua Bengio, backed by 30 countries — the closest thing to an IPCC-style scientific consensus assessment for AI.

safetyEvents.title: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework v2
safetyEvents.summary: Revised critical capability levels covering misuse, misalignment and deceptive alignment, with security-level mitigations attached to each.

safetyEvents.title: Circuit tracing — attribution graphs in a production model
safetyEvents.summary: Method for tracing computation through a deployed model, revealing multi-step reasoning, planning ahead in poetry, and unfaithful chain-of-thought.

safetyEvents.title: Anthropic activates ASL-3 protections for Claude Opus 4
safetyEvents.summary: First time a frontier developer deployed a model under its own elevated safety standard, citing CBRN uplift risk that could not be conclusively ruled out.

adoption.label: Organisations using AI in at least one business function
adoption.note: Self-reported by surveyed executives; up from 55% in the 2023 survey.

adoption.label: US firms using AI to produce goods or services
adoption.source: US Census Bureau — Business Trends and Outlook Survey
adoption.note: A far lower figure than executive surveys, because it samples all firms rather than large enterprises.

adoption.label: Developers using or planning to use AI coding tools
adoption.note: 62% reported actively using them; trust in output accuracy was markedly lower.

adoption.label: ChatGPT weekly active users
adoption.note: Grew from roughly 100M weekly users in November 2023.

adoption.label: Share of US adults who have used a generative AI chatbot
adoption.note: Roughly double the 2023 share; usage skews strongly toward younger and higher-income adults.
